title: Empirical mean concentration for finite laws
statement: Let $\\Omega$ be a finite nonempty set equipped with a measurable space in which every singleton is measurable. Let $p$ be a probability mass function on $\\Omega$, and let $g:\\Omega\\to\\mathbb R$ take values in $[-1,1]$. For a positive integer $m$ and $\\varepsilon\\ge 0$, draw $m$ independent samples from $p$. The probability that their empirical mean differs from the integral of $g$ with respect to $p$ by at least $\\varepsilon$ is at most $2\\exp(-m\\varepsilon^2/2)$.
hypotheses_covered: $p$ is a probability mass function on $\\Omega$
